newsitem.title: USA: Commonwealth sees end to inventory cuts.
newsitem.headline: Commonwealth sees end to inventory cuts.

text.p: Commonwealth Aluminum Corp said Tuesday it is beginning to see indications, including stabilizing material margins, that customers have substantially completed their inventory adjustments.
"Although these early signs have not translated fully into order flow, they do brighten the prospects for strengthening business conditions in 1997," the company said.

Commonwealth said management is evaluating ways to optimize the consolidation of CasTech Aluminum Group Inc, acquired Sept 20, adding the company expects to record a fourth quarter charge releated to the restructuring efforts.

The company said it expects the after-tax charge to total between $6 million and $9 million and cover the assimilation of these new operations, including issues related to product planning, distribution, production, and personnel.
It said the CasTech acquisition is expected to be accretive to Commonwealth's earnings in 1997.
In addition, the company's larger size, increased product and market diversification, and enhanced technological capabilities are expected to reduce earnings volatility.

Commonwealth said its third quarter results were highlighted by higher sales volume, reversing the trend seen in the first half of the year. Sales totaled a record 168 million pounds, up 20 percent from 1995's third quarter, puting nine month sales 5 percent ahead of the 1995 pace.
Commonwealth said it continues to gain in market share against the backdrop of an overall sluggish market.
The company said its third quarter income before an extraordinary item in totaled $4.6 million, down from $7.6 million in the year-earlier period.
Net sales for the quarter were $170.1 million compared with $160.3 million in the same period last year.
